name: What if my bathroom door is too narrow for accessibility?

mainEntity.name: Can an existing bathroom doorway be widened without rebuilding the whole bathroom?
mainEntity.text: Can an existing bathroom doorway be widened without rebuilding the whole bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: A narrow doorway is one of the most common barriers in older bathrooms, but it can often be solved without a full gut of the entire home. Contractors may widen the rough opening, reframe part of the wall, or install a pocket door to eliminate swing clearance problems. In some cases, a barn-style or sliding door can help when wall depth or plumbing makes a pocket door impractical. The biggest constraints are structural walls, hidden pipes, and wiring. If the bathroom is already being remodeled for accessibility, doorway work should be considered early because it affects circulation, fixture placement, and code compliance. A wider doorway can dramatically improve access even before other features are added, especially in compact Los Angeles homes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, in many homes the doorway can be widened by re-framing the opening, changing the door swing, or switching to a pocket or barn-style door. The feasibility depends on wall structure, plumbing, electrical lines, and available adjacent space.
